- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model may overreact; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overconfidence.  
- When sentiment oscillates between 0.27–0.80, model shows mean-reversion bias — adjust forecast to align with 3-period rolling average of true values.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day from day 1–7.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.27” (negative sentiment), model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for pessimism.
